reviews.title: Subscription required
reviews.text: Wouldn't recommend this app while it's a great concept and interface. You shouldn't have to pay for something so simple. Going to switch to a different app that's a simple countdown.

What’s the point of this app only allowing 18 and older adults to get help? Are children not seen? Do they not struggle with mental health themselves and actively harming themselves? Instead of letting kids/teens reach out for support in the community, you ban them and silence them from seeking support when they don’t have any, and really this is the only app that seemed safe for them. What if they CAN’T call a hotline for various reasons? What if they want support from someone besides a therapist? What if they have nobody, because millions of kids/teens suffer alone and some have even taken their own lives for this. Let kids seek support, this is cruel to me.

reviews.title: Community Tab Is Worthless
reviews.text:
I like the app for being able to log urges. However, that's pretty much all I use it for at this point. My compulsion is Hair Pulling, but when I go to the Community tab, I overwhelmingly see posts from people with Skin Picking and Nail Biting compulsions. There is no way for me to filter it to only my compulsion. I don't appreciate that all of those are grouped together with no ability to separate/filter them. The point of the Community tab is so that I feel like I'm not going through recovery alone, but instead I only see people struggling with an addiction that isn't mine in a space that I thought was only for my addiction, and it makes me feel even more alone. Please fix this.

Update: one year later and still no Filter in the Community tab. I should be able to filter by my specific compulsion. I'm paying too much money.

reviews.title: really disappointed
reviews.text: I used this app throughout my recovery journey, and after being sober for a long time, I wanted to come back and look at all of my milestones and sober time. I was surprised to find that all of my progress had been reset, even though I was logged into the same account. What confused me the most is that I had reinstalled the app and switched phones multiple times in the past, and my progress was always restored without any issues. Only now did I discover that automatic backups require a subscription. I had no idea this feature had changed, and I never expected my recovery history to disappear because of it. It's disappointing to lose something so meaningful. Recovery milestones carry a lot of emotional value, and having them erased without a clear warning feels discouraging. I genuinely loved this app and found it very helpful, which makes this experience even more upsetting.

reviews.title: Community Posting Problem
reviews.text:
I greatly value this app & I use it everyday, but there’s a persistent issue of posts in the community section not going through that needs attention. It’s been reported multiple times & support has only offered the suggestion that the post might “violate the community guidelines”, however I’m well aware of the guidelines and know this is not the case. Maybe it’s an error from an automated flagging system, but if so there’s still no way to access the post after hitting submit to save it or request a review. They suggest that we can “log out and log back in”, unfortunately that didn’t work. Considering how important community is in overcoming any addiction, it’d be really great if they could take it seriously and work this out. Any story you post is at risk of going straight into a void with no notification to the user about why it wasn’t posted, and no way for the user to recover the post if they wanted to save it. I pay for premium too which is just salt in the wound since it’s advertised that premium allows you to “backup your data”, but cant back up your data if it’s not even being saved. I’ve asked others on the app as well & I’m far from the only person experiencing this.

I’ve never reviewed an app before, but my attempts to contact support for help on this don’t seem to be amounting to much. I feel a little silly getting so frustrated over an app but when you’re writing a letter to your community after a relapse/during an urge in search of support, and your letter just

The app works well and has good counters. 

I used to really like the community pages and comments but sadly being in the uk I can no longer use them as the app makers have made no effort for people to verify their age. It has been months now. 

Firstly they should be disputing the need for age verification as younger people need access to recovery spaces as much as adults do. 

Secondly it takes very little effort to link with a verification website like other companies did on the drop of a hate when the rules changed. 

It feels like rather than putting a little effort into making sure the app serves everyone that they have chosen to leave some users out.
